utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We have not much time available, so therefore I urge everyone to work as efficiently as possible. First I'd like to deliver a statement on behalf of the Chamber. It is a short statement on the Prosecution's tendering of new documentary evidence. As the Prosecution is aware, its case should have been brought to a close last Friday. We are therefore currently operating in extra time, which the Chamber has exceptionally granted to the Prosecution to hear certain witnesses. There are limits to the Chamber's flexibility. The Chamber has noticed that the Prosecution is using this extra time to -- to clear its desk, so to speak, through a lot of motions, a large number of documents, tendering them into evidence. At various occasions, the Chamber has said that it's not primarily interested in having documents loaded on it but that it requires the Prosecution to carefully select those documents or passages that are important and relevant enough to merit being tendered into evidence. We have also emphasised that we prefer to have evidence introduced in a meaningful way in court with proper contextualization and explanation by witnesses who are in a position to do so. This last-minute attempt by the Prosecution to flood the Chamber with a lot of documents is not what the Chamber will accept, and we are trying to stop this. The Chamber hopes that this gives the Prosecution sufficient notice of what the Chamber considers proper conduct between now and the final day of the Prosecution evidence, which is set at the 20th of November, that is, next week Tuesday. I'd like to add two examples to this statement. We received an announcement that the -- it's not more than that at this moment -- an announcement that the Prosecution would seek to have added to its 65 ter list an expert report on ballistics, on ammunition mainly. It's -- it's two minutes to 12.00 and an expert report to be introduced at this very moment would trigger lengthy litigation, responses, time limits to be taken into consideration. Now, the report as it was provisionally provided to the Chamber knows no author. It -- from the report, at least, it's totally unclear where the material comes from, what was the chain of custody. That's all perfectly unclear. We didn't receive any curriculum apart from that in the report the person who produces it says that he's not an acknowledged expert in ballistics, although he has 40 years of experience with ammunition, which is a rather vague expression. Conclusions are, in terms of probability, this kind of material does not assist the Chamber. And I add to this that it focuses on the origin of the ammunition, that is, where it was produced. Now, where ammunition is produced may be a relevant factor to consider, but certainly is -- does not allow for many conclusions, especially not in a case where there is at least some documentary evidence that a party to the conflict may have considered to buy ammunition at a place where it would suggest that it might be ammunition as usually bought by the opposing side in the conflict. That's one example. So therefore, before the announced intent becomes reality, the Chamber would very much like the Prosecution to keep this in mind. Another example is a Prosecution motion to add one document or, as the Defence says, two documents into evidence. These are handwritten statements of not entirely clear origin. There -- no good cause has been shown why these documents should be added to your exhibit list at this moment, and apart from that, the Chamber also has difficulties to understand what the statements, apart from repetition, add to the evidence that is already in front of it. I -- I can immediately give a decision on that last -- that last motion that the request to have it on the 65 ter list is denied, which, of course, also have consequences for admission of these documents, if this would still be sought. I'd like to move into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. And I could invite already Madam Usher to see whether the witness is nearby, because what we have to deal with will not take much time. Defence counsel are now finally called upon to say whether there's any objection against P1228, the picture of two ladies, as an exhibit to the Dunjic evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Three times no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that makes altogether five times no, three from you. Then P1228 is admitted into evidence. Then P1202 is admitted into evidence as well. The Chamber has heard the submissions on that. The Chamber has decided that P1202 is admitted in its entirety into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Krasniqi. Good afternoon, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may be seated. I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. I do not see Mr. Pestman to be present in court. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The -- the change in the time when we would start this afternoon may not have reached Mr. Pestman. Nevertheless, we'd like to continue. You know what I said yesterday to you, that if an answer to any of the questions might --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you remind me what last night's questions -- question was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was not a question, but I told you that if in answering any question you would be afraid that you would incriminate yourself, then you could address me and ask whether you would be relieved from answering that question. From what I heard yesterday until now, that moment has not arrived. If you would have any such issue, we might even invite Defence counsel then to postpone that question until Mr. Pestman has arrived, but we'll see how matters develop, because I -- it could be that it's out of oversight --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll make it absolutely clear that judging by the intervention yesterday afternoon, the territory I'm going to cover will almost exclusively be territory that would have triggered Mr. Pestman's intervention. But I'm -- I'm -- I understand that the Trial Chamber following that intervention has explained the position to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so I'm perfectly happy to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber also has an -- will have an open eye for any such situation to arise. Yes. Then, Mr. Emmerson, the Chamber would very much like to see whether we can conclude with this witness altogether in one and a half hours, and that would be five-quarters of an hour for the Defence, which is a little bit less than you asked for, a little bit of time remaining for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I will take a moment at an appropriate space to have a word with Mr. Guy-Smith to ensure that, particularly with this witness, that time is allocated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, the question that I put to you at the end of yesterday afternoon - and I'll just get the terms of it precise, if I may - was whether when you were spoken to by Mr. Dean, the prosecutor in Kosovo, in January of 2006, whether you were told then by him that the reason that there was a suspicion against you was that you had -- the prosecutor had information that two men had been seen taking Sanije Balaj into the woods. Did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if he told me that, but the truth is that there were two of us in the car but the person who took her out of the car was Idriz Gashi and she did not resist or do anything against going with him to the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to be absolutely clear, you didn't get out of the car at all; is that -- is that your evidence, Mr. Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't get out of the car at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I just want to make sure, please, that I've also understood your evidence properly about the process by which Sanije Balaj was stopped and taken in for questioning. And I want to put a series of questions to you for -- for which I hope we can get clear and short answers. When you first saw Sanije Balaj near to the Barane headquarters, you were with Ahmet Ukaj; correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were sitting and there was Ahmet Ukaj, Hysen Ukaj, and other policemen sitting under the shade of a tree when we saw Sanije Balaj accompanied by two soldiers who were taking her inside the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And how far away from her were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 40 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I've correctly understood, the two soldiers who were taking her in, you didn't know who they were?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not pay attention to what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, you saw her being walked in. Could you see the faces of the men that took her inside?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were taking her in the direction of the school where the command of the army was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you see their faces?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Before she was taken inside the building, did you see your brother, Mete, in the area at all?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see him at all that day in connection with Sanije Balaj?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What about your cousin Iber? Did you see him that day?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him. I don't remember seeing him that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you -- you, if I've understood your evidence correctly, you had nothing to do with stopping her. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had nothing to do with stopping her.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You didn't take her out of the car.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you didn't speak to her cousin, Hazir Balaj, about her or the reasons why she'd been stopped; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And you didn't take her yourself with your cousin Iber in to see Commander Nazif Ramabaja and Cufe Krasniqi, did you?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And am I right in understanding you were never inside the building where she was being questioned at the time that she was being questioned?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. And I was not interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And she was inside there, you told us, for between an hour and an hour and a half, and the first time you had any contact with her was when she was brought out by Galani; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And during the time she was inside, to your knowledge, the only people in that building with her were Cufe Krasniqi and Galani; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took her to the school where the barracks were, and then later they took her to the building where Shkolla e Kuqe was, the police was, and I could see from the windows, inside the windows that Cufe Krasniqi was talking to Sanije Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. But you never went inside at any point while that questioning was going on, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then you say Galani came out with a notebook and with Sanije Balaj, and shortly after that he ordered you to drive her to Gllogjan; correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Galani came and went inside and Cufe Krasniqi was there when Galani went inside. They spoke with each other there, and Galani came out with Sanije Balaj and a notebook in his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they talked about in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not asking you that, Mr. Krasniqi. We've understood what you're -- you're saying about this incident. But it was when he came out with the notebook and with Sanije Balaj, that was when he ordered you to drive her to Gllogjan for questioning. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And you told us yesterday that you obeyed that order because he was claiming to be your superior; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You said yesterday in answer to the question: Why did you obey his order? Answer: "Because I couldn't say no, because he was my superior and I had to obey his order." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Whoever else he might have asked to do something for him, everybody there would have obeyed his order.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When he suggested to you that Sanije Balaj might have been taken to Gllogjan, were you aware that on the 12th of August there was a massive Serbian offensive taking place in Gllogjan and that the KLA had been routed from Gllogjan by the 12th of August and the Serb forces were there?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, we've seen evidence in this case, including a film, of Serb forces attacking and taking control of Gllogjan and Irzniq on the 11th and 12th of August. Sanije Balaj disappeared on the 12th of August. The question I'm asking you is: Were you not aware by the 12th of August that Gllogjan was under sustained Serbian attack and had indeed been invaded and taken control of by the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask, please, that without it being displayed to the public, 65 ter number 2154 be shown on the screen, which is ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does it need a number, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is, I think, a 92 ter statement about to be given a number. The Prosecution has tendered it. I don't think we yet have an exhibit number for it, but it is a 92 ter statement. And may I enter private session for just a second to explain to the witness whose statement it is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "About 50 metres from the school" -- I'm reading to you now, Mr. Krasniqi. "About 50 metres from the school which served as the KLA barracks, three or four soldiers came out on the road, which was very narrow as it passed through the village. One of them was Mete Krasniqi and he signaled to us to stop. He spoke to Hamdi, who was in the driver's seat. He asked where we were going, and when we answered, he said that Sanije could go no further with us because she has to be questioned. Hamdi said, 'No, she is with us.' Hamdi and I got out of the car. Avni Krasniqi, who was standing next to a white Mercedes minivan behind our car and I went to speak to him. He showed me a black notebook with names of people whom he said had to be interrogated and said that she could not continue with us. I saw Sanije Balaj's name, along with many other Albanian names. I told Avni Krasniqi that if anything happened, he would have to deal with us."

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you complete your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I've completed reading the section to you and allowing the translation to catch up. First of all, Mr. Krasniqi, was your white Mercedes minivan present when Sanije Balaj was stopped?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you speak to the person who made this statement and show him a notebook with Sanije Balaj's name in it?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have any kind of notebook with any names on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, we've heard --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can remove that from the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've heard testimony in this court from Cufe Krasniqi. He is related to you and is a cousin; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just going to read to you a passage of his evidence about the stopping of Sanije Balaj. He said: "That day" -- and I'm reading from 5771, line 14 onwards. "That day I was in the school. The school was called Red. It was a new building. In that building, I was with Nazif Ramabaja. We were talking together about something. We were in the new school." Question: "Then what happened? Answer: "Then two soldiers came. They knocked on the door. After they knocked on the door, we told them to come in. Question: "Who were they? Answer: "They were two of my cousins, Avni and Iber Krasniqi. Question: "What did they say to you? Answer: "They told both of us Nazif was -- Nazif was the commander. They said that there was a person who had been detained by the military police and that person was a suspect. They wanted somebody to come and interrogate that person." Did you go to Nazif Ramabaja and Cufe Krasniqi to ask for someone to come and interrogate Sanije Balaj?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I will tell you that these are Cufe Krasniqi's lies. This says here "on the 14th," while Sanije Balaj's incident was on the 12th. How can you say here "14th" and how can he say "the 14th" when it happened on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, you misheard. I said it was line 14 of the transcript. Cufe Krasniqi testified that you and your cousin Avni came in to speak to him and Nazif Ramabaja to say that a woman had been detained. You say that's not true?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: A little further on, page 5772, line 7, he was asked: "Did he tell you what this person was suspected of, why she was a suspect?" And he replied: "Yes, they said that they had stopped this person while going to Peje. Her goal, according to them, was that she wanted to buy a telephone with an antenna. However, she would go from Strellc to Peje through Rahovec and that was more difficult than going through Lugu i Baranit, Cellopek and Trucuja [phoen]. So the reason she took this other route were the basis of their suspicions." Question: "What did they suspect her of? Answer: "They found a notebook in her possession. She had some addresses on the notebook. They said that they knew her and that they suspected her of working for a Serb, his name was Corovic Dragan." Again, do you remember any conversation with Cufe Krasniqi along those lines?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. And that day I did not see Cufe or meet him. I only saw him inside the office speaking to Sanije Balaj and to Idriz Gashi. And whatever they spoke about in there, I don't know. At least, I don't know. I don't know about other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. A little further down, same page, line 22, he was asked where Sanije Balaj was when this conversation with you allegedly took place, and he replied: "She was in the old school. We called it Red School. It was an elementary school. In that school, there was the police, the headquarters." And he was asked: "Did you go there with your two cousins to see her?" And he said: "Yes, upon receiving the order, I went together with my two cousins, we went directly to the school." Again, we can take it, can we, that that must be untrue as well?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He went on to testify, Mr. Krasniqi, that when he got there with you and your cousin Iber, Sanije Balaj was inside a room sitting on a chair with a soldier he didn't recognise. And after asking her some questions, he decided that she was to be released. And I'm going to put a short passage to you from 5775, line 10. He said this: "I had nothing to say to her. I told her that these boys suspected her that she was a collaborator of that person. They had taken her. There was also another person with her, but that other person was released by the military police. She had been taken here. Then after I said those two words, my cousins intervened. They said she was not telling the truth." He -- he went on to testify that you insisted - that is, you and your cousin Iber - that Sanije Balaj was not telling Cufe Krasniqi the truth and that he eventually had to tell you to get out of the room but that you stood outside continuing to listen to the conversation. All of that is false, Mr. Krasniqi, is it?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He also testified that it was he who asked you to drive Sanije Balaj to her home.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who do you mean "he"?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Cufe, Cufe Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me to take her home?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'll read you exactly what he said. This is 5779, line 23. "Later she refused to come to lunch. I repeated once again my invitation. I told her that the vehicle had gone to take lunch to other places. And then I told her that when the vehicle would come back, we would accompany her. She said no. And then I asked the other people there who were present if they had a vehicle. They told me that they had a red Golf." Question: "Are you referring to your two cousins, Avdi and Iber Krasniqi? Are they the people you are referring to? Answer: "Yes. Yes, of course. Question: "Where did she go? Answer: "She said she knew them. 'They will take me home.' That's what she said."

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they spoke about when they were in the office. I only know when Galani came out from that building with Sanije Balaj with a notebook in his hand. I have no idea what went on inside there. You are asking me the same question over and over again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that's a fair comment. So far as Cufe Krasniqi is concerned, you've told us that he released her, to your knowledge. Correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you have any problems in your relationship with Cufe Krasniqi which might account for the fact that he's told lies about you like this?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No conflict at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we move on, please, to a slightly later portion of your testimony where you described stopping the car on the orders of Galani. I just want to ask you to help us with this, if you can, please. Had Sanije Balaj said anything during the journey between the time you left Baran and the time that you stopped the car?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: She only spoke to Galani and asked him whether they could speak tete-a-tete, and he said "yes," and we drove -- I drove on, and Galani said, "Stop here." I stopped. Galani got out of the car. Sanije Balaj got out of the car. And she did not refuse to get out. Everything was normal. And 40 seconds later I heard the pistol shots and I couldn't even believe that it happened. It was so fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So let's see if we can understand that a little bit more, Mr. Krasniqi. On the way, you say Sanije Balaj asked Mr. Galani to speak face-to-face. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: A private conversation.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What did you think she meant by that?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so when you stopped the car for them to get out, does that explain why you didn't ask anybody what they were doing, ask Mr. Galani what it was he had in mind?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What did you think he -- he was going to do taking this woman into the woods?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that they had some private conversation and they would return, and 40 seconds later the murder happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that came, then, as a total surprise to you because you remained in the car thinking they were going into the woods for a chat. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And the -- the boys that were there, the shepherds that were nearby, I just want to see if you can prompt your recollection, Mr. Krasniqi. When you testified in the trial in Kosovo, you said that they were only about 5 or 6 metres away from you.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never said 5 or 6 metres away from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And when you heard the shot, did you get out of the car then?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Galani came out with a pistol in his hand, I opened the door of the car and I said, "What happened?" And he said, "Don't move, because you will suffer the same fate." And I stopped right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let's move on, then, please, to the quarrel that took place between your brother Mete and Galani a little later on in which you told us that Galani said to Mete he had killed Sanije Balaj and that they had an argument.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was that on -- was that on the same day or a later day?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same day, that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you were asked some questions about this yesterday and you told us you don't know whether that conversation happened in Vranoc or Baran; correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you remember Judge Orie asking you yesterday - this is 10740, line 14 - you -- he asked you: "You describe a situation where your brother and Galani are quarreling and, as you said, in the presence of policemen. Now, were you present when this happened?" And you said "no"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And you were then asked by Judge Orie who told you about it. And you said: "When Mete came home, he told me about this, that it happened like this." Correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then you were asked: "Did anybody else tell you the same story, or was he the only one who told you?" And you replied: "No, it was Mete, but I also heard it from other people, but I cannot remember who was from the policemen there when they had that conversation." Correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, when you were in the Detention Unit here, having been brought here from Kosovo, did you receive a copy of the suspect interview that you had given to Mr. Dean in January of 2006?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you read it?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in that interview, you also say, don't you, that this quarrel took place but you were not there and Mete told you about it; correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You were then asked about this when you gave evidence at the trial, Mr. Krasniqi. And for those following on the transcript of the trial, it's pages 17 and 18. And you described this quarrel that had taken place between your brother and Galani, at which Galani had confessed. And you were asked this: "You just" -- this is the prosecutor asking you questions at trial. "You just described for the Court a discussion and an argument between Mete Krasniqi and Galani; correct?" And you replied: "The source of this dispute was the fact that Sanije Balaj was killed." And then you were asked: "Were you personally present during this conversation or did someone else tell you about it?" And you -- please -- please wait.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't present.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Please wait, because the answer you gave, Mr. Krasniqi, at the trial, on oath, in Kosovo was: "This is a discussion where I was physically present." You were then asked: "I believe that when I asked you about this conversation in January 2006, I tried to clarify with you whether you were present there physically or whether Mete Krasniqi told you about the conversation." And you were asked if you remembered that. And the prosecutor said to you: "I tried to establish whether you learnt this dispute between Galani and Mete Krasniqi because Mete Krasniqi told you about it." And you replied: "I remember very well having been questioned about this detail. I'm a bit afraid in case anything is missing from the translation. The translator was Albanian. I'm telling you the truth today." And then the trial judge asked you that: "You were present?" And you said: "Yes." And a little later on in the trial, Mr. Krasniqi, the trial judge returned to this issue and asked you again about the fact that in your interview with Mr. Dean you'd claimed to have been told this; whereas, you were testifying that you'd been present during the conversation itself. And he asked you: "Are you positive now in court that you were present during the verbal clash and you heard everything that happened." And you replied: "Yes." Now, Mr. Krasniqi, what is the position? Did that conversation ever take place?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the quarrel happened. There are many mistakes here of interpretation and maybe misunderstanding, because that night when the quarrel happened, I was not present. I was present on the next day. And then the day after that when they quarreled -- because this went on, and because of this quarrel, the body was taken away from where it was. So the statement about the first night has been confused with the statement about the other nights.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Do you know why it was that on oath before the Trial Chamber in Kosovo you said that you had been present during that conversation?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first night?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The conversation that was specifically put to you about the first quarrel between Mete Krasniqi and Galani in which Galani admitted to Krasniqi that he had shot Sanije Balaj.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat it once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you help us at all -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, in the portion you just read, I'm trying to find where reference is made to a first discussion or a discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. It starts on page 17 of the trial transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I haven't got the trial --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- transcript in front of me. But could you please -- because that may be true, but I'm trying to find at this moment on our transcript where this was read to the witness, mainly in order to avoid any further --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- misunderstandings.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it somewhere in the portions you read? And if so --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll -- I'll check the marked portions that I've read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because it starts at page 23, where I think the first question was: "You just described for the court a discussion and an argument between Mete Krasniqi and Galani." And then the answer of this witness at that time did not indicate which argument it was. And then it went on: "Were you personally present during this conversation?" I'm just trying to find out -- to understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- how specific these questions were in relation to the first evening, where the witness has testified now --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that there have been several.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I think the best way to deal with this would be for the Trial Chamber just to have in front of it a copy of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of course, it doesn't exist in Albanian, so there's no point in the witness having it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just trace it through?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I was trying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. But at the same time, of course, it's important that the witness understands --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- also now what is put to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of course. And I -- and my concern is to try to take it as short as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you referred us, as you said, to page 17?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: 17 is the first reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think I -- for reasons of time, I was trying to take the shortest possible passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But I'll take it slightly more fully for the purposes of the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And before I do, Mr. Krasniqi, the argument that took place on the night of the shooting, were you there or were you not?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So if we pick it up at page 17 just halfway down the line, halfway down the page, the question from the public prosecutor: "So later in the day, you told us Galani came to your house in Vranoc, which was the headquarters. Answer: "Yes. "Who else was there? Answer: "I remember that Mete Krasniqi and Iber Krasniqi were sitting there. When Galani approached the place, Mete Krasniqi asked him, 'Where is that person? Where did you take her?' Galani told Mete Krasniqi that he had taken her to the headquarters in Gllogjan. Mete Krasniqi said to him, 'You did not have any reason to take her to Gllogjan headquarters.' Then Mete and Galani got into a dispute. Mete said, 'You do not have to take her to Gllogjan, because she was released." After they exchanged some insults, Galani said, 'I have killed her myself and you have nothing to do with that.' After which Mete asked him, 'Where did you kill her and why did you kill her?' Galani then said, 'This is my problem. If somebody goes looking for her, tell them that I have killed her. You are allowed to tell them that.' We were, four of us, Galani, Iber, Mete, and me. Question: "Up until this point, had you told anyone what had happened at the forest that day? Answer: "No." Please wait.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I to answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Please wait. Question: "You just described for the court a question and an argument between Mete Krasniqi and Galani. Answer: "The source of this dispute was the fact that Sanije Balaj was killed. Question: "Were you personally present during this conversation or did someone else tell you about it? Answer: "This is a discussion where I was physically present." The transcript then follows with the witness being confronted with his earlier inconsistent account and concludes with the presiding judge seeking clarification at the bottom of that page, where the witness says: "I am telling you the truth today." "That you were present? Answer: "Yes." So the whole passage refers to an argument that took place later that day when Galani allegedly came to the witness's house in Vranoc and where, as the first answer makes clear, the witness was claiming that he was there together with Galani, Iber, and Mete. So I put it in a rather longer form. Mr. Krasniqi, you told the Trial Court in Kosovo that you'd been present at this row on the night of Sanije Balaj's killing with Galani, Iber, and Mete and you were given a number of opportunities to clarify it, and each time you repeated that you were present that night, the first night. Why did you do that?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present only at the moment when I was taken to go and bury the person. This -- this is what I've said several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say now you were present only when you were taken to go and bury the person. So you didn't hear the conversation being spoken. We are clear about that, are we?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they had a quarrel in Baran, I was not there. When they came to Vranoc, I was there. When Iber Krasniqi came and Galani came to take me with them and bury the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you just --

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this is where a quarrel took place between Mete and Galani. But I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we'll just, finally for the sake of accuracy of the record, complete this by going to page 46 of the transcript, where the judge comes back to it. And just below halfway down the page, your testimony - these are your words - when you're asked about why it was in your interview you had claimed not to have been there, as you are now claiming not to have been there, you were asked about that inconsistency, and you said: "Maybe it is a problem in translation or there was a mistake with the interpreter." You then said this: "The night when the murder happened was the night when there was a verbal discussion." The judge asked you: "Are you positive now in court that you were present during that verbal clash and you heard everything that happened?" And you replied: "Yes." Now, Mr. Krasniqi, either the evidence that you've given us today is false or the evidence that you've given -- gave on oath in Kosovo is false. Correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've not been lying here or I've not been lying in Kosova as well. But you are misunderstanding. You are confusing the questions. You are just asking how many the times I've drunk water and how many times I've eaten. I have said it several times. When they had a quarrel in Baran, I was not there. When they came to Vranoc, I was there and they were quarreling why the person was killed. This is what I've said. What I was -- I am asked here, I was not asked in Kosova in this -- in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. I'm going to move now to ask you some questions about the time that you spent in Switzerland before you entered Kosovo, Mr. Krasniqi. First of all -- and I'm conscious that Mr. Pestman isn't here and has indicated the desire to raise objection to the line of cross-examination I'm going to pursue, but I'm in the Trial Chamber's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do it the following way: You put a question to the witness. You ask the witness to -- Mr. Krasniqi, the next questions that will be put to you, wait first before you answer them until I say you can answer the questions. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, were you convicted of any offence, that is, found guilty and sentenced by any courts in Switzerland for criminal offences whilst you were there between 1990 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may answer this question, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have never been convicted and I've never been arrested in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to ask you whether in 1991 you were aware then of criminal allegations being made about the beating of your wife.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Or in 1992 to 1993, criminal reports against you for robbery and burglary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I interrupt for -- for a while. Mr. Pestman, the Chamber was under great time pressure. And at the last moment -- yes. At the last moment we had to change the time schedule. We reminded Mr. Krasniqi of his rights to address the Chamber if any question would be put to him which, if answered in accordance with the truth, would incriminate himself. We now came to a point where Mr. Emmerson asks a few questions about the -- what happened in Switzerland. Mr. Emmerson asked him whether he was ever convicted, where Mr. Krasniqi said he was never convicted; and one or two follow-up questions were there as far as police reports. On this part, I instructed the witness to wait to answer the witness [sic] until I had invited him to do so. I invited him to answer these questions. I think my role ends here. I don't know whether there's any role for you, but just to update you. Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Before you proceed, I'm -- I'm very unhappy about this situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: I was under the assumption that -- in the assumption that we would start quarter to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're not in any way blamed for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can tell you that the developments which finally resulted in a change of starting time, I think I said yesterday that the picture changes every 15 minutes. I would now reduce that to every 5 minutes. And the Chamber was unhappy with it as well, and I tried to pay special attention to the issues for which you are here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure I'm -- I've understood what -- what has been asked and what topics have been discussed, but the -- the Swiss court case or the conviction --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't say anything about a Swiss court case until now. The question only was whether Mr. Krasniqi was ever -- whether he was ever convicted. No further details were given at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know -- I take it that you have not discussed matters with him. So therefore, you are already revealing something that the witness might not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Whether I have discussed this with my client is confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: I will not reveal whether I have discussed anything --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You needed permission to discuss anything --

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: No, certainly not before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not before, yes. Of course. Of course I leave that open at this moment. If --

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Yes. But I would like to express my discontent about the way this has been developing. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Yes. And I also -- I have no idea what the last question was, but I would seriously advise my client to remain silent, not to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it depends on whether an answer to a question could possibly incriminate him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's something we'll decide on the basis of every question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, when did you leave Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pestman, it -- it might assist you if you read the last, I would say, 15 lines of the transcript before you entered court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Can I -- can I ask one question before I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It depends on what --

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Maybe my client can take his headphones off before I continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please take your headphones off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pestman.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Yesterday we discussed the issue of the -- the judgement or the alleged conviction in Switzerland. And one of the questions I raised was whether this conviction is revocable or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: And as far as I know, this matter has not been resolved yet. So I was wondering whether the Prosecution would be able to inform me about that -- or the Prosecution or the Defence would be able to inform me about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The questions until now were about procedures in Switzerland, not about the substance. I think the questions were, but if you'll read the transcript, you'll see that. Let me see if I can find it. It starts page 32, line 2. And if you would read that, then you'll see that the questions were about awareness of Mr. Krasniqi of convictions and reports, police reports brought against him, which, of course, does not deal with the substance of the allegations contained in either the judgement or the reports. Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think the witness needs to replace his headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please put your headphones on again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My -- my question was: When did you leave Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, please, the -- the question before this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, my -- I think that was the last question I asked you: When did you leave Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please explain once again from the beginning. Can you explain the first question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, the -- the question that is put to you - forget about any other question at this moment, because if there's any unanswered question, it is implicitly withdrawn - when did you leave Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have left Switzerland on the 17th of July, 2001. That's why I wanted you to repeat the first question, because before I had a problem with the question that was related to the problem I had with my wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Forgive me. Let's -- let's be clear. You left Switzerland on the 17th of July of which year?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And from that point onwards, were you in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've -- until the 15th of July, I was supposed to stay in Switzerland, because I was married there. And when I was having some private problems with my wife, then there was an order issued by the court. And three days before leaving Switzerland I have -- I have taken the money from the bank, according to the rules in Switzerland, and two days before -- this was done two days before leaving Switzerland, according to the order issued by the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see. Please pause for a moment and remove your earphones for a second.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I would propose now to move to ask the witness questions about the outstanding arrest warrant and judgement in absentia. But I asked him to remove his earphones rather than put the question, lest Mr. Pestman has an issue about him even being informed of this information and how that might affect his legal position. I see there isn't one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pestman.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Well, the question I raised is still pending, whether this conviction, if there is one, is irrevocable. We have to assume it is not. And therefore I object to any questions I cannot -- if I can object.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: But I would certainly advise my client --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's -- let's try to get things clear. If the judgement is not irrevocable, that means that everything the witness says about any of the defence we find in the charges might add or might be used in evidence against him under the relevant law of procedure in the Swiss canton we are talking about. Now, the awareness of a judgement is not evidence which incriminates. I could well be aware of a judgement where I think that the judgement was rendered upon false testimony. So therefore awareness of the judgement as such, Mr. Pestman, seems to me - but please correct me when I'm wrong - seems not to be knowledge which, when it becomes available, would be incriminating as such. Of course, I am aware that if the judgement has not yet become final, that it may have consequences for asking for review of the case to be retried. But that is not as such an answer that would incriminate. So therefore -- but please tell me if my analysis in this respect, you would disagree with that -- that would not be an answer the witness should not -- would not be a question the witness should answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: I'm afraid I have to agree with your analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson. And, Mr. Emmerson, you're also invited -- I look at the clock. I said five-quarters of an hour, and we are 58 minutes now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I agree entirely with Your Honour on the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, are you aware that there is an arrest warrant in Switzerland against you following a conviction in your absence for involvement in armed robberies?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never been informed about what you are asking me about. Never in my -- in my life I've ever been convicted. Well, you can go and ask information from any country you'd be interested to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really sorry -- sorry you're considering me like a robber, because this is something I've never done in my life. I had a civilian life, a private life before, prior to the war and after the war, and I've never been involved in robbery cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, just so that you understand what the position is, I am putting to you the contents of documents that have been provided by the Swiss authorities with your photograph on them that show that you were convicted in September 1995 of a series of offences of robbery in people's homes whilst they slept, and sentenced to seven years' imprisonment. So what I'm putting to you is the contents of an official Swiss document. Now, the question I'm asking you - and I think you have answered it - is that you are unaware that you have been convicted in Switzerland? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have no information of this kind, and I don't think there is a reason for me to be convicted in Switzerland. No reason for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are all your questions. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is your pleasure that I start now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How much time would you need approximately?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, if we rush it, I could probably finish it in 15 or 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm also looking at the interpreters. Would that be -- if you rush, you're not telling us that you're speaking more quickly so that it is done at the expense of the interpreters. If you promise that, I think we could continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I won't speak more quickly then.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, you're aware of the fact that Idriz Balaj was prosecuted in 2002 in a famous trial called the Dukagjin Trial, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that he was being prosecuted, there were many newspaper articles about that trial, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You read those newspaper articles, didn't you, because it was of interest to you, having been a FARK soldier and the trial being about the death of FARK soldiers; correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've not read them, because I was not interested to read these articles, because I had my life to think about. And I've been working at the Italian military barracks and I had no interest in dealing with such matters. I was never interested in such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we please have 2D001836 up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does it need a number, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, it does, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be MFI D221, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Because it's a newspaper article and it's -- there are some - I don't know what you call them - transmission problems, we have the article in hard copy, which has a -- is clearer, which we can give to the Chamber just for purposes of viewing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the original we can't read anyhow. But if enlarging on the screen would not be sufficient, then it -- I think it would be rather the witness who would need to see the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Go to the second page of that document, please. [Microphone not activated] And if we could have it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'd prefer that the witness be provided with a copy which is better legible than what we see on the screen at this moment. At the same time, Mr. Guy-Smith, where the witness testified that he didn't read the newspaper articles, of course, one can wonder what it brings us. But we'll see what your next questions are.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you would take a look at what's been marked for identification as D221. Do you see that in front of you? And looking at the -- the headline of that article, does that headline include the name of Idriz Balaj and also the name of Togeri on it?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is the information, that information that Idriz Balaj was also known as "Togeri," information that you had when the Dukagjin Trial was going on in 2002?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we could now have up on the screen 2D001858. Once again, page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does it need a number as well, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, that's also going to need an MFI number. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be MFI D222, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know what we are going to do with newspapers, Mr. Guy-Smith, but the previous question could have been put to the witness without showing him a newspaper article, which has not been established that he ever read it and where the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not necessarily done with that particular article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't object to their tender into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, in e-court of the previous document I have no translation. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you see the picture before you in what has now been marked for identification? You've seen that picture before, haven't you? That was a picture that was shown throughout newspapers in Kosovo and also on television during the Dukagjin Trial.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the newspaper article that I showed you that had the name of Idriz Balaj and Togeri, that's a newspaper article that you've seen before; right?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that one not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the Dukagjin Trial, you saw newspaper articles that had Mr. Balaj's name and the name "Togeri" associated with it, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I explained earlier I worked in a military barracks in Peja and I could not go in and out whenever I wanted. I started work at 7.00 in the morning and -- and when I left work, it was just half an hour to reach home. And -- and when I went home, sometimes I saw the news, sometimes I didn't, because I was not interested.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness speak closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My question was: You saw newspaper articles --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, could you come a bit closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, do you want me to repeat it, what I said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, there's no need to repeat it. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My question was: You saw newspaper articles with the name Idriz Balaj and Togeri associated with each other during the Dukagjin Trial, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I haven't seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During that period of time, you had information, you were told by others that the name of Idriz Balaj was associated with the name of Togeri, as you've just told us; correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you had an opportunity to discuss the matter of the body of Sanije Balaj being moved with the prosecutor in Kosovo; correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did you say? I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My question is: You had an opportunity, you spoke with the public prosecutor in Kosovo concerning Sanije Balaj's body being moved; correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you testified at a trial concerning that matter, the movement of Sanije Balaj's body; correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in your testimony during the trial, you were asked the following question by the public prosecutor and you gave the following response: And this is on page number 23. Question: "Do you remember one of these individuals going by the name of Toger? Answer: "Now when I follow TV broadcasts of The Hague trials, I recognise him as Toger. Idriz Gashi knows better." That's what you told the public prosecutor then; correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you testified yesterday, you told us that the first time that you saw Toger was when he came up and parked in front of the school and spoke with Galani; correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been misunderstood, because it wasn't the first time that I saw Toger. I saw Toger during the war and not only that day. This is a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The first time you saw him with regard to the movement of the body was when he came up to the -- when he came up and parked in front of the school; right?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you saying that it was the first time that I saw him, that I recognised him, or what was the question? Can you repeat that again?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, what I'm saying is with regard to the movement of Sanije Balaj's body, you told us yesterday that Toger and others, two other people who you were not able to identify, came up and parked in front of the school and spoke with Galani. Correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday and I am saying it today again: Toger came with Idriz Gashi; they came together up to the school. Idriz Gashi asked me to go with Toger to disinter Sanije Balaj; whereas, Idriz Gashi remained in Baran. And for my security, I took Iber Krasniqi with me, and I've said it several times, and this is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My question is: That happened at the -- at the school. And that's the school at Baran; right?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It didn't happen anywhere else now, did it?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm looking for a specific document. It will take me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you were speaking with the prosecutor in January of 2006, what you told the prosecutor at that time was that the meeting, the first meeting occurred on an asphalt road while you were at a police station; correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was it -- the police station is at a different place than the school now, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. In your first statement concerning this matter, you identified another one of the people who was involved in assisting -- in the movement of the body, and that was a person by the name of Bujar Haradinaj; correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were asked a series of questions about that in 2002 in an -- in an UNMIK interview also; correct? Do you remember that? In December.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you were specifically asked who was involved in the matter, and you specifically indicated that Bujar Haradinaj was involved in the matter as one of the people who helped move the body; right?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that -- that there was Bujar Haradinaj, but when I saw him in Peja, then I -- I said that there was a different person, then I realized that it was a different person other than Bujar Haradinaj who was there. And I've said this to the office of the prosecutor in Peja.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You've never seen any photographs of Bujar Haradinaj on television, have you?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You made a mistake in 2002 when you mentioned him as being one of the individuals involved in this incident, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I thought initially that it was Bujar Haradinaj, but it wasn't him. There was a mix-up with another person.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you went to collect Sanije Balaj's body, you told us yesterday that you wrapped it up in a blanket. Correct?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that was something that you personally did; true?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me, Iber Krasniqi, and two other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the blanket that you -- you wrapped it -- you wrapped the body up in, do you remember that blanket? That was a -- was that a brown blanket?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was her body when you wrapped it up in that blanket fully wrapped up as if you rolled -- rolled her body fully in the blanket so that the blanket kept her body intact?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before -- before Mr. Guy-Smith goes on, I just want a clarification. I didn't object at the time, because I was looking through the -- through the transcript. At 45 -- page 45, line 14 he said: "When you testified yesterday, you told us that the first time that you saw Toger was when he came up and parked -- parked in front of the school." I can't find that in the transcript. Could perhaps Mr. Guy-Smith point to where in the transcript Mr. Krasniqi said it was the first time he saw Toger.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He -- I -- he didn't say it was the first time. He said that he saw Toger --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- let's move -- let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The thrust of the question dealt with whether it was at the school or the crossroads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I said "let's move on," because we're already at 21, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I suggest to you, Mr. Krasniqi, that you are mistaken when you say that Idriz Balaj was present at the time that you moved the body with Idriz Gashi and two other people.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you saying? Can you repeat that once again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, what Mr. Guy-Smith tells you, that you made a mistake when you said that Idriz Balaj was present when the body of Sanije Balaj was moved. Do you agree or do you disagree that this was a mistake when you told us that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I suggest to you, Mr. Gashi [sic], that after you saw Idriz Balaj in the Dukagjin Trial you made a determination that you were going to exact whatever form of revenge you could because of your belief that he had killed some of your fellow colleagues who were FARK soldiers.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. That's not the cause. Because those who were killed, they were not colleagues of mine. I'm sorry what happened, but they were not my colleagues and there's nothing to take revenge against. But the truth is what I've said. And what happened with the Dukagjini Group, I'm not interested in that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm going to further suggest to you, Mr. Krasniqi, that you and Idriz Gashi were involved in the death of Sanije Balaj. And that -- and that you are not telling us the truth with regard to this for a number of reasons, not the least of which is your concern that you owe a blood debt to the family.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I -- I'm not in blood with that family. As Shaban Balaj has stated here, we went -- that we've asked for Avni, and he was hiding from us, that's -- that's not true. That's a lie. Because I have never hidden away from Shaban Balaj, because we owe nothing to him and I will never hide away from him and from no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, you said 15 to 20 minutes. We're now at 25. Could you please wrap up now within two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, I'll leave it there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Re, any --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I have no questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, Mr. Harvey. There is nothing in this field which is similar to customary -- let alone customary law. Mr. Re, how much time would you need? Should we have a break now?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's just one matter I wish to ask him, and that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be five minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that do then? I'll limit you to five minutes. Mr. Krasniqi, we'll have a break. We will resume at 25 minutes past 4.00, and then your examination will presumably not take long any more. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, you'll now further -- be further examined by Mr. Re. Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, Mr. Guy-Smith asked you about where -- the place where Toger picked you up from when you went to exhume the body. I just want to clarify: Was the military police place you were speaking about, was that in the school?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The school -- there were two schools, the Red School and the White School. The White School was the military barracks; whereas, the Red School was the military police barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Secondly, Mr. Guy-Smith raised the issue of your knowledge of Toger at the time when he picked you up from the school and took you to exhume the body and wrap it in a blanket and you drove off with it. You said you -- you'd known Toger in the war and it wasn't the first time you'd seen him. How many times had you seen him before then, and in what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war, I saw him many times. I -- I only knew him by name "Toger." I didn't know his full name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was the -- do you remember when the first time you saw him was? How long was it before that time when he picked you up to dig up the body?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. Probably one, two months before. I can't remember accurately.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But you said you saw him during the war many times. Where did you see him? What was he doing? In what circumstances did you see him during the war?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen him in bad circumstances, but that was the last time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I didn't ask you about bad circumstances. I'm talking about how many times you'd seen him and where, doing what. Can you just confine yourself to that, please.

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I saw him in the headquarters, when I went to the General Staff, on the road many a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which -- which headquarters are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Gllogjan headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was he doing there when you saw him in Glodjane headquarters?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the other thing I wanted to ask you about to clarify was: Mr. Emmerson asked you about the meeting which you said you heard about on the night when you -- when Sanije Balaj was killed, a meeting between your brother, Mete, and Galani where they quarreled. Was that the only meeting that you knew about that they quarreled -- the only meeting they had in which they quarreled after she was killed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness answered this question already. He said that there was several evenings, not only the first evening. Let's hear from the witness. I'll find it for you. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
