utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who is -- who is to speak now?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that the only meeting they had where they quarreled about Sanije Balaj and what had happened?

utterances.speaker: AVNI KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I said it earlier. I've said it several times. But I'm saying it again. In -- in the Baran school, when I was there -- when they quarreled there, I wasn't there physically. But when they came back home and Mete asked me, "What happened to that woman," and I -- I told him what had happened and that we -- we got to bury her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any -- is there any need to -- further questions triggered by the re-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, we have no further questions for you, but this Chamber, before we -- we'll thank you for testifying in this court. The Chamber will have to withdraw for a short second because we were informed that a motion has been filed. The Chamber will adjourn, but most likely for a very short period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: --- Break taken at 4.37 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is only two minutes ago that the Chamber was competent to deal with the contempt case against you, Mr. Krasniqi, a contempt case in which you are an accused, not a witness, that the Chamber received a motion. That Chamber consists of the same Judges as in the Haradinaj case. Those Judges have considered that motion, and by way of -- I don't know whether that exists by courtesy oral copy. Since you are in this courtroom and since the Prosecutor is in this courtroom as well and since your lawyer is in this courtroom, you are informed that that Chamber decided to grant that motion. The motion is Prosecution's application to withdraw an indictment for contempt against Avni Krasniqi. That motion is granted. And the decision will be put in writing. But for practical and logistical reasons, the Judges of which that Chamber and this Chamber is composed, thought it would be good to inform everyone right away. That means that the -- that consent is given to withdraw the indictment, and that has a consequence for you -- your detention as well. That Chamber also decided that you should be released immediately after the necessary practical arrangements are made by the Registry. Mr. Krasniqi, I now address you again as a witness in this case. The Chamber would like to thank you for -- well, to say "to thank you for coming" is a different matter, but at least the Chamber thanks you for having given your testimony in this court, having answered questions put to you. We would like you to follow Madam Usher, who will escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, are you ready to call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I am. I anticipate that Mr. Sadri Selca is available somewhere very nearby to testify. And if he is, I call him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are you aware that there is another witness waiting to finish his testimony and that today is the last day? So therefore, please keep that in mind. There's no way that the Chamber will sit tomorrow. There's no way the Chamber will sit on Monday. Tuesday has been reserved for a videolink testimony. So therefore, use your time as good as you can. We are now quarter to 5.00. We need another break. That means that altogether we have still 2 hours and 15 minutes. I take it that the gist of the decision on Witness 1 which has been -- has been explained to the parties might have some relevance for the time the further examination of Mr. Versonnen would take. I specifically ask you, Mr. Guy-Smith, how much time do you think you would need for the cross-examination of Mr. Versonnen? And I add to that, without the usual ritual dance steps which we sometimes observe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I've always been trained to follow my -- you know, my tradition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Since I underestimated the time with the last witness and could have used some more time, I don't want to underestimate my time here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I had offered Mr. Re some agreed facts with regard to issues that had been previously discussed in this trial. They are relatively discrete. I think there probably is little, if no, dispute about them; however, for reasons that Mr. Re knows best, he was not in a position to agree those facts. But that does require that I go through discussion with him, Mr. Versonnen, about practices and procedures that he engaged in with this witness. And I have reduced the examination probably by somewhere in the neighbourhood of at least 50 per cent. I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that still --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think -- I'm telling you what I've done --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- in preparatory remark so that when I give a time at this moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's already half.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- The time-- it's already half. And I believe that it can be in 20 minutes, assuming the answers are as crisp as the questions that I hope to ask without the ritual dance, which is going to make me uncomfortable, because that's what I know how to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I also take it that some of the concern is that evidence by Witness 1 might be introduced through Mr. Versonnen, that was one of your major concerns, that has been diminished. And that therefore -- I think we are talking about paragraphs 14 to 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That most of the issues there --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's going --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- do are not -- are not that relevant any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's going to be -- it's going to be directly to policies -- it's going to be directly related to practices and policies used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then is -- could we expect any agreement on the 92 ter statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't believe so. I'm -- I'll be -- I'll be -- it's really very simple, Your Honour. He was part of the team. He was aware of certain practices and policies that had been promulgated by the -- by the Office of the Prosecutor, by the ICTY. That's D119 and D120. He didn't follow those policies and procedures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which doesn't mean that a 92 ter statement for that reason alone would not be -- we'll --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, because it examines -- it examines that some of the -- it examines some of the specific issues with regard to D120 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm happy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm happy to give another go with Mr. Re, because I quite frankly think that we could -- we could agree, because these are really issues that are not -- they should not be in dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. For me, agreement on a 92 ter statement is something totally different from cross-examining Mr. Versonnen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm in total agreement with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On some --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The matters that I'm talking about with regard to cross-examination - thank you, Judge Hoepfel - are those matters --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to apologise for the speed at which I was speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, my question mainly is, although I expect you to thoroughly cross-examine the witness on that, Mr. Guy-Smith, whether paragraphs 14, 15, and 16 of the 92 ter statement would still need objections. Then, Mr. Re, I wonder whether paragraph 18 of the 92 ter statement is a paragraph you would press. I do not expect an answer immediately, but if you would give that some thought over time, and it might -- you might interpret that also as -- not as guidance but that the expression of these thoughts might give an indication of what you could expect. Then let's move on to the next witness, which is Mr. Selca. I do understand that there are no protective measures sought.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Re, you are aware that the Chamber will then -- after the Chamber has asked other counsel how much time they would need for cross-examination of Mr. Versonnen, Mr. Emmerson, how much time would you need in addition to what Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of Mr. Versonnen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: None. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, I think with the guidance of the 92 ter statement, more or less, that the whole testimony of Mr. Versonnen should not take more than half an hour, including cross-examination, and therefore be aware that we need another break and then we'd have to start not later than five minutes to -- 25 minutes past 6.00. And then -- [The witness entered court].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I first should apologise. Could you put on your earphones.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Selca, do you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Selca, you are -- you appear here as a witness in the case against Mr. Haradinaj, Mr. Balaj, and Mr. Brahimaj. Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration; that is, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text will now be handed out to you by Madam Usher. I would like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Selca. Please be seated. Mr. Emmerson, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, I wonder if the witness might rather prematurely remove his headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take off your headphones for -- for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I ask Mr. Emmerson to be brief. I know what he's going to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But we're running out of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, what I'm going to say is this: We received notification at 13 minutes past 4.00 from the Prosecution of 17 documentary exhibits that it proposes to use with this witness, 5 of which have been tendered and marked not admitted, and 12 of which consist, so far as I'm concerned, nothing more than 65 ter numbers, in the sense that they might be on the 65 ter list, but with that sort of notice it is obviously impossible to assimilate the material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The position is that the witness statement of this witness has no exhibits attached to it. And in those circumstances, I object to the use of exhibits with this witness. I obviously --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Under normal circumstances, we'll take some time to further discuss this. I'm afraid that in the present circumstances, that, Mr. Re, when putting certain documents to the witness, is at risk that on considering later whether we should admit those documents - and, of course, also therefore pay attention to the -- to the related testimony - he takes then risks. The Chamber cannot at this moment use the remaining two hours spending 55 or 60 per cent of the time to the procedural issues, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is on the record -- it is on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Mr. Re has certainly heard the statement earlier today by the Chamber, and Mr. Re will certainly be aware that using his time as efficiently as possible might put certain -- well, requires some decisions and choices to be made. Yes, Mr. Re. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I join.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I start?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You can start. But demonstratively looking at the clock could have started at earlier stages of this proceedings. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Headphones. Headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Your name is Sadri Selca. You were born on the 27th of October, 1956, and you were born in Baran, and you are a serving police officer in Kosovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You are also an accused yourself of a contempt charge here. I'm not going to ask you any questions relating to the contempt charge. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then perhaps I add to that at this moment, Mr. Re, that present in this courtroom is also Defence counsel that has been assigned to you, Mr. Dieckmann. Mr. Dieckmann's role here is limited to issues of your right not by answering questions to incriminate yourself. That might not be perfectly clear. Mr. Dieckmann, the procedure is that if you would like to intervene for these purposes, that you should address me. Then we'll ask under those circumstances the witness to take his earphones off. And then you can address me to seek permission to advise your client on matters which then you'll first explain briefly to us. Then we --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: May I just briefly once more ask Mr. Selca for your full name and your date of birth. Because it was not understood correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My full name? Sadri, surname Selca. Born on the 27th of October, 1956. Place of birth, Baran, municipality of Peja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just some personal details. Did you work as a -- a -- did you do JNA military service 1979 to 1980? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. And you worked as a police officer in -- from 1981 to 1990, then from 1990 to 1998 you worked as a schoolteacher in chemistry and biology. Are those details correct?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: These data are correct too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you join the FARK, F-A-R-K, in Kosovo during the conflict in 1998?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you join one called Brigade 3 in the village of Barane in July 1998?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was the commander of that brigade Nazif Ramabaja, with his deputy being Esat Ademaj, and the assistant commander, Musa Dragaj?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: He was exercising the -- the task of the commander because the proper commander couldn't be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The two other brigades also based there, commanded by Tahir Zemaj and Musa Gjakova?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes, one was in Prapaqan. The commander was Tahir Zemaj. And the other one was under the command of Musa Gjakova.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you based in the school in Barane?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Accurate, at the school of Baran. That's where we were deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What -- what did you do? What was your job?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: I was responsible as an intelligence and counter-intelligence officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What unit would you describe yourself as being in when you were in intelligence and counter-intelligence?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: I was in the 3rd Brigade in Baran.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just tell the Trial Chamber what you mean by "intelligence and counter-intelligence." What did you do? What were your duties and who you reported to?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: The general commander was Nazif Ramabaja, but my tasks included to find out about the movements of the enemy and all the rest that was related to defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who -- who assisted you with that? Who were the other counter-intelligence and intelligence people working in Barane school?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I've had the greatest cooperation with ordinary citizens. They helped me a lot and then I reported to my superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was anyone else working with you in your intelligence activities at the school, or were you the only one?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: No, I was the only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you carry out investigations in the course of your intelligence work?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: It was very difficult to carry out investigations because the situation was such that we couldn't undertake investigations properly and all the investigations were based on hearsay, what I heard, what he heard. And then you -- you took it from sources which you thought were reliable, but there was no proper investigations as such carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you obtained information, how did you record it?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Once I received information, I typed it. And that information was passed on to my superior directly. And then it was worked on the basis of that information if that was -- if that was true, then we took measures. But on the whole, mainly we -- we have failed in -- in corroborating what we heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You typed -- you said you typed information. Was the information on -- in what form was it typed, please.

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: The classic typewriter. Not a computer. It was a classic typewriter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were these reports you wrote or the typed information, were they numbered or filed or categorised in any way? What order did you have to maintain the records of what you typed?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Due to the circumstances, all the information didn't have numbers but they were passed on to superiors and some -- some were kept, some were handed over to the superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you keep copies of them?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Usually I did, but when we withdrew from Dukagjin after the Serbian attack, those documents were all destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you sign these reports or typed information reports that you did?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Normally all documents that were written, they were signed by myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your information about who Ramush Haradinaj was in July 1998 and his relationship with the unit in Barane?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: As regards Ramush Haradinaj, with the commander of Baran they had very good relations. Excellent. We had mutual cooperation. I, for myself, I was at a lower rank. I -- I was not all across the relations with my -- between my superiors, but I thought they had very good relations at the start.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At the start.

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: At the beginning, with the -- at the beginnings of the KLA, together with Ramush, we took the oath in Baran.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mete Krasniqi, who was he?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: As for Mete Krasniqi, I think personally, and the people who know him, he was not involved with -- on the military side of things, but he cooperated with both sides. So I'm not clear about his position.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. In -- in the statement you made on the 16th of October, 2002, you described him as a commander --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I'll withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Absolutely. I think Mr. Re knows full well --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I withdraw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's withdrawn. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there a military police unit or brigade in Barane when you were there?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes, the barracks was at the elementary school. That's where we slept. The kitchen was there. That is -- the logistical base was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Maybe I didn't say it, but I meant to say "military police." Was there a military police brigade or unit in Barane?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was running that?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, the military police, a part of it was -- was deployed in the elementary school and it was led by Hasan Gashi, and I was in charge of it too. The other part, the so-called military police about which I don't know much. I don't know who led them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was Mete Krasniqi in either of these military polices, the one under Hasan Gashi or the so-called military police which you don't know much about?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: At the beginning, Hasan Gashi led that unit. But when the -- the barracks was -- was established, then Hasan moved to the military barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Selca, can you please look at me. Okay. Please listen to the question. The question was about Mete Krasniqi, no one else. Okay?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, Mete was not in the military brigade in which I was operating. He was a self-employed policeman, but he was not part of the brigade where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the other brigade? You said there was another one called the so-called military police. Was he part of that one, do you know?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm sorry. As far as I know, that formation was led -- the military police was led by Hasan Gashi; whereas, me, Sadri Selca, was responsible for intelligence and counter-intelligence. And -- and the -- the military police was under my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about Toger, Idriz Balaj? Did you know him at the time?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, personally I didn't know him. But on the basis of rumours and speculation, I heard that a person from Gllareva has come here voluntarily to fight in Dukagjin. And I didn't know more about that person. But somebody else may know more about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about several people whose names appear in a statement you gave: Sanije Balaj, Istref and Nurije Krasniqi, Zenun Gashi, Qamil Gashi, Dede Berisha, Skender Kuqi, Azem Gashi, Misin Berisha. All right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, this list is rather long. I tried to figure out how much time there would be left if the Chamber would equally divide the remaining time among the two parties. You would have another 18 minutes. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Sanije Balaj.

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. What happened to her?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: What happened to her? I learned from her brother, whose name is Shaban Balaj, I think - I'm not sure about that - but that's his family name, Balaj. He came to the barracks in Baran and -- and then told me that his sister was missing. After some time, I worked in that respect to investigate the case, and I got some unverified information that she was drowned -- she was killed and disappeared together with the materials that she was -- she possessed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who asked you to investigate that? Or why did you investigate it?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: It was her brother personally who suspected that someone from other -- someone from some forces -- he didn't have any specific suspicion. Because she was in Malisheve, some 50 kilometres from Baran, and that's where the suspicion lied [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to show you an exhibit. It was -- was P897.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I just wonder whether Mr. Re --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- might clarify that last answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No I don't have time. I'm sorry. If I had time, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to show you an exhibit, MNA -- which is marked not admitted, P897, which is an official note dated Barane, 26th of August, 1998. And it has your signature on the bottom of it and it relates to Sanije Balaj. First of all, I want you to identify the document and tell us whether it's a report you prepared and what were the information -- where did you get the information which was in that report.

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Thank you. For this case, I will tell you that that information, it was late evening when I met Sanije's brother, who -- who asked me whether I knew anything about his sister. At the time I said, "Let me go into the barracks and see if anyone knows." When I came out of the barracks, I understood that no one knew about it, but then an honest citizen came to me late in the evening and told me that she's been killed, she was -- she was raped, and then she was killed and then buried. And he didn't want to mention names who had done it. At the end, it was understood that that was -- that was carried out by people who the Tribunal is aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. In the middle it says: "In all probability Togeri then took her to Lake Radonjic. She was executed because she admitted to working for the Serbian police." It's your document. How did you get that information? Why did you put that piece of information in that report?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: This information was given to me by those people who were close to her and they knew the circumstances, and that's what they informed me about. And I didn't have the opportunity to -- to process the information. So whatever I got, I wrote it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next -- the next one I want to show you is Exhibit P898, marked not admitted. It's a -- a statement of the 28th of August, 1998 said to be taken -- taken by you. Present Rexhep Krasniqi, a statement given by Hysen Ukaj, Ahmet Ukaj. It has your signature on it. I want you to very briefly tell the Trial Chamber the circumstances in which you took it, very briefly. Because this is a statement that you took from Hysen Ukaj and Ahmet Ukaj.

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: It's true, Your Honours, that this information I got by the people that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'm going to ask you now about Istref, Kujtim Imeraj, and Nurije Krasniqi. What do you know about what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: First I'd like to say that my courier, a close associate of mine, he was from Junik. He lived in Turjake and he had relatives there. One morning he told me that they have taken them. He was describing to me how these elderly people were taken. Then I was trying to find out, irrespective of -- of their ethnic or religious affiliation, I found that those people were kidnapped by one person who is currently said to be outside Kosovo, in some Western country, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was that that you received this information?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, for reasons which you all know - and Your Honours and the people who are here present --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: -- we have not been able to keep this piece of information. But time has been --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please. Please look at me. I will stop you if I want you to stop. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, can the witness please be shown 65 ter Exhibit 749. Please look at me when -- so I can direct you when I need an answer or not. This is a document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It needs a number, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: 65 ter Exhibit, sorry, ter 749.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 749. It needs a number, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI P1229, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's coming on the screen. It's dated the 25th of August, 1998. It's described as an official note saying that you had been informed by an informant that Istref Imer Krasniqi and his wife have been abducted from Turkaj [phoen] village by Rrustem Tetaj and their fate is unknown. And it bears your signature. Is that what you were referring to? And does the date help? And is that your document?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: That's accurate. This information -- this note was written by me, and at that time I had quite a lot of bits of information to tell me what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Was there --

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: That he was pivotal to what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Was there a soldier, Fadil Maloku?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Unfortunately, that witness has died. But it was said that he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you speak to him? Please look at me. Look this way. Did you speak to him?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: I spoke to Fadil.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: About what had happened to that couple; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: No, no. For this, I spoke to a young man who lived there. Otherwise, he was my courier. His name is Naselje Kuqi [phoen] from Junik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was any information given to you about Idriz Balaj in connection to that, with that?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: According to the conversation that I had, it was said that Rrustem Tetaj took them in a vehicle. As to who carried out the -- the kidnapping, I was not able to get any information on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In a statement you made in October 2002, you said you spoke to a soldier, Fadil Maloku?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me. He's given you an answer. Are you now impeaching him?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm asking him whether he said that and if so, is it correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, no, that's what's known as impeachment, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll leave it till the end, then, if I have time. But the Trial Chamber is aware of what's in the statement, so I'll come back to you --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, sir. Excuse me. I object. And I think it's totally inappropriate for Mr. Re to do that, to --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm talking about the time I have left available. Can I please continue. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Whether you have no time left or not, does not mean that you can't comport yourself in a particular fashion, sir, and I object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No more quarreling, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I please move to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. You're moving to your next question, Mr. Re. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Exhibit -- it was 896. It was marked for identification -- sorry, MNA. It was marked not admitted. I wish to take the witness to the eighth page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the passage I want to take you to is paragraph 19, that says: "Imer Krasniqi from the village of Turjaka, Peja was taken for an interview regarding his collaboration with the Serbian police and several other cases." What can you tell us about that? Are these your notes?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Look, the Krasniqi couple -- I don't know, maybe this piece of information may be, but they were in a very poor economic state. And the Serbian police frequently returned as to how much they collaborated with them, I don't know. I don't believe very much in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But they're your notes?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. They're my notes. But to tell you the truth, although I come from that area, I have lived there very little. And when I visited --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Stop. Stop. Look at me, please. The question was: Are they your notes? Yes or no? The answer is "yes." I'll now move on. Okay?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes, they are my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you write in your notes that Mr. Krasniqi was "taken for an interview regarding his collaboration with the Serbian police and several other cases."

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I do not accept this to be part of my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Whose notes are they?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Somebody else may have written that, because in that office it was a public place. Everyone could enter and then go out of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The document -- if I could just hand you perhaps a hard copy of this, it might be quicker. The front page, it says "Sadri Selca." The next page, it says: "In charge of the brigade, Sadri Selca, official notes." It's item -- item 19 at the end. But -- all right? Now, do you recognise those as official notes with your name on the front; correct?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Official notes with your name on the front. Okay? Correct?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes, that's true. My name is at the top. And I believe that I thought that piece of information at the time was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you think it was correct at the time? And why was it written in official notes with your name on the front?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Look, that -- I must say that there is a -- a distance, 3, 4 -- of 4 kilometres, and these people were in very poor economic state at home, they were elderly, and someone -- for -- for --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please the question was not that. The question was: Why did you think it was correct at the time and why was it written in the official notes with your name on the front? Address that question, not another one, please.

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Accurate at the time. I got the information that probably that could have been accurate at the time from the source that I got that piece of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Moving to Zenun Gashi. Was he a friend of yours?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: We worked in the police together.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Was he Roma?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes, he was Roma.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he continue working in the police up until sometime before the war?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes. We left the police in 1990, but he continued because his family was poor and he carried on -- with agreement from other friends, he decided to continue work in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How was that viewed by the KLA, the fact that he was working in the police?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I object to the form of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened to Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've withdrawn the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened to Mr. Zenun Gashi? When was the last time you saw him. You've described your statement in July 1999 [indiscernible] for the last time?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: I saw Zenun Gashi for the last time at the centre of Baran when I was there with some friends. I saw a car where he was in. And -- and as he knew me, he asked me if I could give him some water. And so I did. I offered him some water.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was he doing in the car? Whose car was it? And what -- what -- who else was in the car?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I didn't know the people who were in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they civilians or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: No, they were civilians. We didn't have uniforms. Everybody wore what he could, what he had. There was no unified uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Selca --

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Especially with the group that were with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Selca, you've sworn to tell the truth here, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes., I've -- I've taken an oath to tell the truth to justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Think carefully about whether -- whether the people in the car were wearing uniforms or not, please, and think about the statement you made earlier.

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I -- I'm not trying to dodge the truth, but it's a long time that has passed since. And during this time, I've had some psychological traumas. So I cannot remember every detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Tell me -- tell us the state that Zenun Gashi was in the last time you saw him.

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: When I saw him last, he was in a very poor state. He was beaten. He asked me for water. I took water to him. I went to -- to the house in the village which was closest -- closer than my house. I got some water. And I gave it to him, and he couldn't speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were the people in the car Albanians or Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes, Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he their prisoner?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was their prisoner or their hostage, but he was in their car.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who did you hear they were? What was your information about who these people were?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you the truth, I wasn't entitled to ask. I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How about Mete Krasniqi? Did he have anything to do with this?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: I can't remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were these people armed?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: No, I didn't see whether they were armed. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you hear happened to Zenun when he left with these men in the car?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Look, at that time the information was coming from individuals, individual citizens. And -- and what you got, you had to verify it whether it was true or not, because each and every one had their own opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were you told about who'd ordered Mr. Zenun Gashi's abduction?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, it's a long time since and I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, you made a statement in October 2002. Would looking at that statement refresh your memory as to what -- what you heard at the time?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes, if you can give it to me and if it's true, I will -- I will defend the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What you said was: "I didn't recognise any of the soldiers but they were Albanians. They wore camouflage uniforms that I couldn't recognise, but this was normal at the time. Soldiers used uniforms of any kind that they had received from other countries. I talked to the soldiers and told them to release Zenun because he was an innocent man. They replied by saying, 'Here is your colleague' in what that I felt was a threat against me, meaning my time would come. They drove away and Zenun was never seen after that." Does that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: True. Correct. Everything is correct. And I agree with everything that you refreshed my memory about. The same said to me that, "You will suffer the same fate."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, we'll have a break now. You have, as I said I would divide evenly the time available -- I first would like to invite Madam Usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom. We'll have a break, Mr. Selca. We'll have a break for approximately half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, will it be you who ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is one document I would just like the witness to identify, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Oh, no, it's P888, which has his name on it. I just wish him to identify it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's a document signed by him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One minute for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please look at the document which is coming up on the screen. It's dated the 29th of August, 1998. It's a report written by you in relation to Azem Gashi. Just have a look at it on the screen. I just want you to identify if it's a document you prepared and that's it.

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes, this document has been written by me. However, I was not at the place where this happened. I was informed by citizens --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'd like, as a matter of fact, the witness to answer this question. Please complete your answer, Mr. Selca. You said you were not there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. I was not at the place where this happened and the time when it happened. But according to the words, I heard rumours from people who told me about the wounding of Azem Gashi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the end of this report reads as follows: "I received this information directly from the aforementioned person." And you added to that: "But the wounded man himself knows the exact time at which the incident took place." This suggests - at least, this report suggests - that you received this information not from rumours but from the person mentioned there, which is Azem Gashi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But in the beginning I got the information from citizens. But in the meantime, I contacted Azem Gashi and this person sometimes admits it, sometimes denies it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did you ever --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if the -- the answer was unclear or clear to you. Sometimes he said, "I have been wounded by Ramush." Sometimes he said, "No, I was wounded by" -- somebody else. So the information I received from him, I wrote it there. But in the meantime, he changed his mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer, Mr. Selca. Mr. Emmerson. Mr. Emmerson is counsel for Mr. Haradinaj and who -- he'll now cross-examine you. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Selca, I want to start by asking you some questions about Sanije Balaj. When you were answering questions to Mr. Re, the gentleman on the other side of the court, you mentioned something about Malisheve in connection with the case of Sanije Balaj. Can you just elaborate on what that was that you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: When I spoke about Sanije going to Malisheve, she was a person who was a trader. She went to Malisheve for trading purposes. And I don't know any further about her background or anything else. I'm not of her age. I did not know her personally, but I heard these things from individual citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned a suggestion of rape in relation to Sanije Balaj, and you said that -- that in the end it was understood that it was carried out by people that the Tribunal would be aware of. I just want to see if -- if I can ask you a little more about that answer. In the witness statement that you made about the Sanije Balaj incident, if I can just read to you what you said. And I want to see if it helps you at all in your recollection. You -- just -- just bear with me for a moment. Let me just read to you a passage from your statement. You said this: "One military police officer from the village of Vranoc told me about this incident. I cannot remember his first name, but I'm sure his family name is Ukaj. He had been on patrol together with Avni Krasniqi, father's name Kadri; Iber Krasniqi, father's name Tale" -- T-a-l-e -- "and a third officer whom I cannot remember. They were all military police officers. Avni's and Iber's fathers are brothers, so they are cousins to each other. Near the river Bistrice in the village of Vranoc they met a female, family name Balaj from the village Lower Strellc. Avni Krasniqi had stopped the female and taken her somewhere nearby. There he raped her and afterwards killed her by shooting her with his handgun. After this, Avni Krasniqi forced Ukaj to shoot one round at the already deceased body. This, he stated, was done to involve Ukaj in the case and prevent him from talking. They had seen two young shepherds nearby and together with them dug a grave and buried the body." Now, that -- that is a passage from your witness statement. Can you tell us, please, where you got that information from about Avni Krasniqi having raped and shot Sanije Balaj.

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly the names of the persons, but I know that a book that has been written and published, not by me but by other people, the names of the persons who raped her and killed her are there, and then forced the two shepherds to bury her. It was late in the evening when one of these people involved came to me and told me about what happened. A few days later the brother of the late woman came to look for her sister -- for his sister. He came to the barracks --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just pause, because I'm going to ask you about the brother coming in in a minute or two. What I want to understand now: In this witness statement, you describe somebody called Ukaj coming to you and telling you that Avni Krasniqi had raped and shot Sanije Balaj and that another man, called Ukaj, had been forced to shoot a round of ammunition into the body by Avni so that Avni could implicate him as well. That's what you wrote in your witness statement. I just wondered where you got that information from. That -- that particular piece of information. Do we understand that it came from --

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: First of all, I apologise, I did not give this statement. I took this statement from the statement maker. And that's what he told me, because this is not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Fair enough. I understand that. But you were shown earlier on by Mr. Re a statement which had the names of Ahmet Ukaj and others on it which gives a different account, and what I'm interested in: This comes from your statement where you have recorded being told that Avni raped and shot her and then one of the Ukajs was forced to shoot her body too. And it's the information about the involvement of Avni in raping and shooting her that I'm interested in. Where did you get that information from to be able to put it into the statement that you gave to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I can't remember the exact person who gave me this information; however, I remember that it was late in the evening and the brother of the said woman came to me to the barracks and asked whether I knew where his sister was. I said that she's not here, but he insisted and he wanted to know where his sister was. I said, "I know one thing, that she had been traveling from Decan to Malisheve for getting supplies and it's possible she went to Malisheve for business purposes." Later on, I heard that she had been eliminated close to Vranoc village. And I don't have anything further to add to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You -- you mentioned Shaban Balaj coming to speak to you. Again, I want -- just want to put a short passage of your witness statement to you. It reads as follows: "Some two weeks after this, Shaban Balaj came to me and asked me if his sister, Sanije Balaj, had been arrested because she was missing and villagers said she had been taken by the military police. Even though I knew what had happened, I didn't tell him. I only informed him that she wasn't arrested." Can I ask you: Do you remember having a conversation with Shaban Balaj where you chose not to tell him what you knew?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct that I had the information that Sanije had been interred close to Bistrice by some shepherds. But it was the time of war. People were armed, and I didn't want to cause even worse things.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I understand. You also say in your statement that if you remember correctly, he - that is, Shaban Balaj - "managed to recover the body after the war and the family reburied it in their village." Can you help us as to where you got that information from?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: I received the information from the shepherds of Vranoc village. They told me how they were ordered by some persons to go and get shovels and picks and to cover the body of the late woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Let me move on, please, to the cases of -- of Nurije and Istref Krasniqi. You -- you mentioned a man called Naser Kuqi. And the translation that we received was that he was a courier. Am I right in thinking Naselje Kuqi was a postman or a mailman of some kind?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes. The correct answer is that Naser Kuqi was from my village and during the war he lived in Turjake. But because I had some obligations in my office, he was my personal courier.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. I understand, then. Just confirm for us, please: The information you got from him, that was information that he had got from somebody else, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: This information he had heard from some citizens, from some villagers from Turjake, and he -- in the morning he told me that Nurije and Istref are missing, they have been kidnapped.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Just to be clear, that -- the -- do you know the names of the people he got the information from specifically now?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: No, I don't. I don't remember them. At that time, I -- I knew them, but because I did not write them down, I have forgotten them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, the -- the next matter I just want to check with you: You were asked some questions about Zenun Gashi and the time that you saw him. I just want to put one proposition to you from your witness statement in connection with that. You say in your witness statement that you went to see Zenun's family and his wife. I'm sorry, let me put the quotation again. You said: "I went to see Zenun's family, and his wife told me that a group of soldiers had abducted him from their house the same morning that I saw him in the vehicle." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. I met Zenun in the car --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: -- together with some soldiers. The said asked for some water, and I made it possible to have some water for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Forgive me. I -- all I wanted to clarify with you was that when you spoke to the wife, she told you that it was the same day you'd seen him that he had been taken. That's the point. And you've confirmed that, so I will leave the question there.

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Correct. Correct. He had been taken that day early in the morning, about 8.00 to 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And --

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- one other -- one other matter on documents. Mr. Re showed you a notebook and asked you about some entries in it. And it was a notebook that had your name on the front. And at one point in your answers, you said the notebook was in the office and people could come in and write in it. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: I think that every note that I have written down, I accept them as mine. But at that time we did not have enough paper, so maybe some people used my personal notebook for their own notes. However, everything that I have written, I will accept it as mine without taking into consideration the consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sometimes when notes appear in that notebook, you have a name, a first name, followed by a name in brackets, followed by a second name. Can I just be clear. When you put the name in brackets, does that refer to the name of the father?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Correct, father's names, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if we could just go into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That -- that concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Guy-Smith, who's counsel for Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Selca, when you were speaking with Shaban Balaj concerning the disappearance of his sister, he told you that at the time she was carrying a considerable sum of money with her, about 2.000 Deutschmarks; right?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's what he told me. But it didn't occur to me that I had to say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And he also discussed with you the fact that she perhaps had rejected the attention or attractions of certain men who were with her that day; right?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: I would like to say only this: That the night in question when Shaban's sister did not report home, he came to Baran to my house and asked me. At that time I was at home. And he said, "Is my sister arrested? I think that my sister has been stopped by KLA forces." And I said to him, "Let's go to the barracks and see." We went there and we saw that she had not been stopped by the KLA forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you ever find any money that had been with her according to her brother, Shaban, the two to three thousand Deutschmarks?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Pardon, did you say 3.000 Deutschmarks?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Two to three thousand Deutschmarks.

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Keeping in mind the fact that I, as a member of the KLA, did not have the right to search anyone how much money they had, I don't know how much money she had on herself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that this matter was being discussed and being investigated, were you aware of the fact that there was a trial involving Mete Krasniqi and a number of members of his family where the imam from Vranoc, Imam Luqman came, and there was a trial under the Kanun to make a determination of who was responsible for this death?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: During the said time, I did not have any information or knowledge about the case, but the citizens suspected that this had -- was something that had been done by people who were not members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Under the Kanun, are you aware of -- we've heard evidence here before from the brother of Sanije concerning the matter where there is -- excuse me, Mr. Selca. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Selca.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me finish, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. First listen to the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That where the body is not found, the requirement is that where there's no body, there are two blood debts that are incurred.

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I am 52 years old but I know these things very well. However, after this happened, I was informed that night and I said this even earlier, because I was informed --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My -- my question is under -- I'm asking a question about -- since you say you know these things well, under the Kanun, as a matter of Kanun law, where the body is not returned, is the result of that that two blood debts are owed? I mean, you can answer that question "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. However, we are speaking about true justice and not the Kanun here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I have no questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, any questions triggered by the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking you whether you have any questions but whether any questions triggered by cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- just in relation to the investigation of Sanije Balaj --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You were asked some questions. Was there a policeman named Faton Mehmetaj involved in that?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: No. I know Faton. I knew him during the war. But I have not seen him ever since, but I don't think he was involved, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was his -- what was his role, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just -- just bear with me, please. I don't think there were any questions about an investigation. I don't think these questions arise out of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you are speaking about Faton Mehmetaj, he called himself a security officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, where do we find the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I thought it was an investigation. If just -- if I could just ask this one question about that, and if it -- anything -- it triggers anything, I have no objection to Mr. Emmerson asking a follow-up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. No, but that's -- it's not how to extend the examination of the witness but how to finish it. So if you can indicate where such a question was put, then so -- to the extent the cross-examination has triggered the question, then I'll easily --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, it triggered it in my mind. It may be of assistance to the Trial Chamber to find out whether this witness was aware of the role of Mr. Mehmetaj in the military police and who he was reporting to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've got one minute --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you do not give us the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said Faton Mehmetaj called himself a security officer. Who was he reporting to? He was a security officer for who?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: Without trying to politicise the army, I think that there were certain volunteer groups that had two or three commands. However, Faton was from Gllogjan, municipality of Decan. He served as an officer, according to his own words and to the words of other people. He worked in the sector for security and information.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: For who? You said he was from Glodjane. Did he work from somewhere in Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: SADRI SELCA
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I was not aware, because he very rarely came to the area where I lived. I met him several times. We greeted each other. But I don't know the reasons for his travels or what he was doing exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are those your questions, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Chamber will adjourn for one or two minutes for reasons to be explained after we return. --- Break taken at 6.31 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Selca, you have concluded your testimony in this case. You are in The Hague not only as a witness, but you were also an accused in a contempt case. Now, the Office of the Prosecutor has filed a motion seeking approval of the Chamber competent to hear the contempt case, which actually is the Chamber composed of the same Judges as you see here, consent to withdraw the indictment against you. To the extent -- since you are here, it would be very impractical to call you back tomorrow and to inform you about the decision in that case, and therefore, although it is not part of the case in which you just testified, you are hereby informed that a decision was taken on that motion to -- in which leave to withdraw the indictment was asked for. That motion is granted. That means that the Prosecution may now withdraw the indictment against you. And in that situation, you're also informed that you will be released immediately after the required travel documents are obtained and the necessary practical arrangements are made by the Registry. This is just a practical way of informing you, although it has got not directly to do with the testimony you gave here. The Prosecution is hereby also informed about the decision taken by the contempt Chamber. Mr. Selca, I'd like to thank you for having given testimony in this court. You are aware that still practical arrangements have to be made, travel documents have to be obtained, but most likely the Prosecution will now withdraw the indictment against you, because they sought leave for that. Then you may follow Madam Usher who will escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dieckmann, this concludes your role, which has been a role with a lot of silence. Nevertheless, it was appreciated that you were here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And I would like to say on behalf of my client that we highly appreciate that the Chamber and all parties make it possible to give my client a chance to give testimony here. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, your client himself decided that he would give testimony. And if he might have felt encouraged by what happened before, then that was not the -- the sole purpose of these activities. But thank you for your words. Mr. Re, are you ready to call the next witness? Who is Mr. Versonnen, take it? Because I have to inform you that where we had in mind that possibly there would be a videolink still this afternoon, that our most recent information - but you see the information comes by the minute - but let me just read what the newest information is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's -- the parties are informed that there was no way to establish a videolink until well after 7.00 and the Chamber sees no possibility to even start inquiring into whether in that videolink we could receive the testimony of a witness. The Chamber will further consider the matter over the coming days. Of course, this will have effect as well on another matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is, of course, a related issue about a videolink which was requested for Tuesday, the 20th of November. And I'm especially addressing you, Mr. Harvey. We have heard about your concerns. We have also heard about your -- some -- some problems, which we do not envy you to have some of these problems, but the decision of the Chamber is that that request for videolink where we earlier said that the Prosecution could move on to prepare, that request for videolink for Tuesday, the 20th of November is granted. I just give the decision at this moment, reasons to follow in writing or orally, but it's important that everyone is informed about decisions, first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the -- the only matter that gives me some pause still is that you said at line 98 -- at page 98, line 2 that the Chamber will further consider the matter over the coming days. That's in relation to the videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is whether there is at all time available to hear the testimony of that witness, so whether we'll move in the direction of receiving that testimony at all. And I'm now talking about the witness who was for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While not scheduled in the videolink but considered in the videolink.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, I'll have to watch this space.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re -- Mr. Versonnen, first of all, welcome. You may have been waiting the whole of the afternoon. We are sorry for that. Mr. Versonnen, you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The 92 ter summary I wish to read is this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there an agreement on what is in the 92 ter statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, it's -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Because the disagreement, I understand, was about paragraphs 14, 15, and 16. I'm not aware of the -- what the -- the ambit of the decision is in relation to Witness 1. I'm not aware of -- I'm not quite sure about guidance from the Trial Chamber as to whether I could actually ask the witness about what was said in relation to paragraph 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's disagreement on that, the Chamber invites you to elicit -- and I think that can be done in a relatively short time -- to elicit the evidence contained in paragraphs 14, 15, and 16 viva voce. I further could inform you that -- I just have to find it. I further have to inform you that paragraphs 18 and 19 mainly explain why the investigator did something, which does not assist the Chamber to the extent reference is made to what the witness stated at the time. We can read that in the statement itself. So therefore, 14 up to and including 19 are to be elicited viva voce. And we do not encourage you to elicit 17 and 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Versonnen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If -- if I might for purposes of -- looking at the clock, I have a sneaking suspicion that we will not be calling Mr. Versonnen back. Will that -- will we be doing that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we'll try to finish the testimony of Mr. Versonnen today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, we'll see how it goes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Versonnen, in your statement, you refer to showing Witness 1 some photoboards which -- a photoboard. Just tell the Trial Chamber what you did. It was on the 15th and 16th of October, 2002.

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember I showed him a photo spreadsheet containing pictures of eight male individuals. And I asked him if he -- if he was able to recognise any of the persons displayed on this photo spreadsheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were you when you did that?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was -- I was standing next -- next to the -- to this witness in between the witness and the interpreter, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there anybody else with you apart from the witness and the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, there was nobody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Where -- what was the physical location of your showing him the photoboard?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in a -- an office of the Barane police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want to show you 65 ter Exhibit number 117 and ask you whether that is the photoboard which you showed the witness. Is that the photo board in question?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What -- what did you say to the witness when you showed it to him?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if he was able to -- I'm not sure if I'm put -- recognise or identify any of the individuals whose photos were displayed on this spreadsheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did the witness say or do?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At this time, before Mr. Versonnen responds to that question, I would interpose an objection. It is the same objection that was interposed which forms the basis of our 92 quater response. It is hearsay. The gentleman in question is no longer alive. We have no way of cross-examining this person whatsoever. And it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- it poses all of the problems --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It poses all of the problems that were raised in the previous motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that you'll not be surprised where the -- where the Chamber, especially in relation to this event, has decided - although you have not yet received the written decision - to -- to deny the objection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- under specific that the same ruling applies here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I gather --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I gathered that was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is denied. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The question was: What did Witness 1 do or say when you showed him the photo board?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He looked at it and immediately pointed out the person as mentioned in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, what -- you said a person as pointed out in the statement. Did he -- just tell the Trial Chamber what he did in terms of pointing out the person in the statement?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he -- he identified the person he was -- I don't know if I can reveal the -- the nickname of the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Very much so.

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. He was also talking about the person called Toger and he pointed out the photo of individual with number 6 as being this so-called Toger.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said he was -- I heard the words "very -- always talking," but it's recorded on the transcript as "also talking." Did you say "always talking" or "also talking" about the person called Toger?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, when talking about this person, he was always referring to this person with the name Toger.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What do you mean by "always"? What --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Just for purposes, so I don't break Mr. Re's flow, could I have a continuing objection to any statements that were made by the decedent regarding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's understood, Mr. Guy-Smith, that whatever this witness says, Witness 1 says, that it's objected to. And that objection is -- although not yet for the future, but is denied until now. And if that changes, we'll let you know. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your use of the words "always," just explain to the Trial Chamber the witness's -- Witness 1's use of the word "always" -- we're talking about your use of the word "always" when you spoke about Toger?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
