utterances.text: Well, throughout the interview, he mentioned this name as the perpetrator he was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said -- Mr. Guy-Smith is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. -- the word "always" causes no problems to the Chamber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you -- what did you do with the -- did he make any notations on the photo board -- I don't think we've got a number for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you please assign a number for the -- for the document, eight persons, photo-spread which is on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be MFI P1230, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you ask him to make any notations on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At this point, I object to leading. He can say what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, there's a short way of long way of doing it. I mean, he's an experienced police officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please choose the short way, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you ask him to make any notations on the Exhibit P1 -- 2130? ?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because besides this document, the second one was -- the one together -- was together with this document was identifying the names or mentioning the names of the other male individuals on this photo spreadsheet, and I didn't deem it professional to have these names disclosed to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And is number 6 the accused Idriz Balaj?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- that was what -- according to the identification sheet of the photo spreadsheet, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions. Then just to get things straight, are there any objections against the 92 ter statement as it's there up till this moment, paragraphs 1 through 13?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There are not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And 20 through 22?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I had previously indicated that paragraph 20 has within it an implied statement of the decedent. As to the extent it refers to the investigator notes and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- to the extent the investigator notes have any statement from the decedent, yes. There is an objection to 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Objections by the other Defence counsel, 1 through 13 and 20 to 22? Mr. Emmerson, not?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My objection was confined to paragraph 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I have nothing further on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing further on that. We'll decide at a later stage about admission. Would it be you, Mr. Guy-Smith, who cross-examines the witness first?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I think you said 20 minutes or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's try to finish, then, in 20 minutes. I see some positive responses from the booth. I'll strictly adhere to the 20 minutes. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Versonnen, I'm -- I'm going to try to do this very quickly. If you would listen to my question. Most of the questions I will ask you, you can probably answer "yes" and "no" -- "yes" or "no." If you need to explain in any answer, please take the opportunity to do so. But if you'd kindly just initially answer the question "yes" or "no," I think that could get us through a bit quicker.

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You joined the ICTY as an investigator in 1998, did you not?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During that time, when you first joined in 1998, you were part of a team that included your team leader of Mr. Raatikainen. Also on the team when you joined was a gentleman by the name of Pekka Haverinen; right?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct, sir. Mr. Haverinen was not part of the team in 1998, as far as I remember. He joined later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When -- when you were involved in the investigation of Mr. Balaj, a photo board was compiled or a set of photo boards were compiled which your team was going to use for purposes of making identification interviews; correct?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could please have P364 brought up onto the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm showing you in a moment, when it comes up, what has been marked as P364. This is a set of photo boards. There are three in number that were compiled by your team for purposes of investigation; correct?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it bears a ERN number, so it -- I suppose it is correct. The -- I don't recognise the document as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say you don't recognise the document as such, do you recall that a set of photo boards was put together, three in number, for purposes of this investigation?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, I cannot remember, sir. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you would take a look at P364.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if the registrar would be kind enough to go through each one of those pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Looking at those pictures, does that refresh your recollection with regard to the question asked of whether a set of three photo boards was compiled for purposes of this investigation?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I really cannot remember this, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. If you could confirm just for us with regard to the set of three photo boards that there are sequential ERN numbers of U0157619 through U0157621. Can you confirm that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. With regard to the photo boards, to your knowledge were the set of photo boards that were compiled for purposes of the investigation, how many photo boards were there?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know, sir. And -- and for the record, I wasn't involved in the compilation of these photo boards.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they were done by a colleague of mine, but, again, I'm not sure about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would have been Haverinen, would it not?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could have been Mr. Haverinen, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We've heard testimony from Mr. Haverinen that P364 which is the set of photo boards before you is a set that was compiled for the purpose of this investigation. My question to you is: Did you independently have an additional photo board made or go out and have any other kind of photo board made for purposes of your specific investigation with the decedent?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you tell us where you obtained the photo board that you used with your interview for identification purposes, as you've told us, with the decedent.

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I received it while -- while we were on this mission from -- from one of my colleagues, who must have been -- or Mr. Haverinen or Mr. Raatikainen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As you sit here today, you can't recall that.

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm -- I'm not sure. But it must have been one of the two mentioned colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before you became an officer working here at the ICTY, had you engaged in a photo board procedures? And by that I mean, had you engaged in an identification process in your domestic country?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during that period of time, did you receive training with regard to some of the concerns that exist in terms of the kinds of procedures that should be followed with regard to identification procedures because of the danger that is implied in eyewitness identification?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And how long were you a police officer before you started working here at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a police officer since 1986.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you tell us how many times you engaged in photo board identification procedures before you came to the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to say, but maybe on five to ten occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before you came to the ICTY, were you aware of concerns that existed in the justice system internationally concerning wrongful convictions based upon misidentification of individuals?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I -- I -- I am not. I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were not.

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you came to the ICTY, were you made aware of the presence of guide-lines that existed for purposes of engaging in photo board identification procedure, and in that regard I should tell you we have heard testimony that members of your team had received such information.

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- as far as I can remember, when I joined in 1998 we were subject to -- it's called an induction course. And through that induction course, we received a copy of the -- of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we please have D119 brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you aware of the identification guide-lines that had been promulgated by the Office of the ICTY before your arrival here in 1998?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Have you seen the guide-lines that are before you? Ever.

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to reports that are -- were supposed to be filled out when engaging in a photo board identification procedure, were you given any guidance or material concerning such a report?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I would ask that D120 be brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Looking at D120, the document is entitled "Photo board identification procedure report." The first line indicates "the name of the ICTY investigator conducting the procedure." And it follows from there.

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could -- I cannot remember this -- this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like you to take a look at page 2 of the document and specifically at paragraph 9 of that document. And I'd like to ask you: Independent of whether or not you have ever seen this specific report or whether you have no memory of it, whether or not during the time you were with your team a discussion was had that it would be important for a photocopy of the photo board, whatever number it was, to be signed by the witness, the interpreter, and the investigator adjacent to the photograph that has been identified.

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, again, as far as I can remember, this was never discussed in the team, but the reason why it wasn't initialed by the witness and the interpreter was, as I explained before; I didn't want to disclose the names of the other individuals on this attachment to nor the witness nor the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I appreciate your answer, but -- but please do help us, if you could. Looking at P -- at what has been marked for identification as P1230, that exhibit consists of two pages with sequential ERN numbers of U0031022 and then a second page, which is independent, which has what I believe to be the names of the individuals, which is the page that you're concerned about. My question to you, sir, is: You did not follow, obviously, paragraph 9 with regard to the actual photocopy of the photo board, which is P1230; right?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did so for the reason I explained before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's not my question. You didn't -- you didn't do that; right? There's no information contained on this particular photo board which is memorialised so that the Chamber or finder of fact has an independent ability to make a determination of the accuracy of the statement that you've made here with regard to the decedent pointing at a photograph. There's no mark. There's no signature.

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But it's incorporated into the statement which is signed by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. Guy-Smith, why not put this to the witness. It's -- it's clear that there's no signature, that there's -- otherwise, it would have presented to us, I take it, by the Prosecution. If this is the -- what is attached to a statement, then if there's no -- nothing on it, then it's not there. So -- so certainly interesting to see, but hardly of any use to ask the witness. I mean, it would be surprising if he says it's there, where we can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, maybe he -- maybe he used invisible ink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. If we would litigate on the basis of such assumptions, Mr. Guy-Smith, then I'm afraid that we should reserve another two years. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Going back to D119 for the moment, which are the identification guide-lines. Did you factually obtain any information concerning the physical description - and by that I mean weight, height, hair colour, facial hair, any remarkable characteristics - of the individual that the decedent was referring to?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, I -- that, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Did you make any notes with regard to where you were standing, where the witness was, and where the interpreter was at the time that you engaged in the photo board procedure?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. The only notes I took are reflected in this specific statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I -- I note that the -- that the photograph of Mr. Balaj is in position 6 in P1230. Do you know how his photograph came to be in that position on that particular photo board?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: You are now speaking of which photo board, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: 1230, the photo board which is part of the documents that are attached to Mr. Versonnen's 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: One of the three; yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, only one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The other documents were in P364, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- a set of photo boards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, I -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- that were compiled by Mr. Haverinen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before you spoke with the decedent, were you aware of the fact that Mr. Balaj's likeness had been spread over the television and in newsprint as a result of his involvement as a defendant in what has been called the Dukagjin Trial?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As you sit here today, you have no memory of having information that Mr. Balaj had been involved as a defendant in the Dukagjin Trial.

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I -- I said that at that moment when I met the witness, I -- I don't know. But I -- I heard about this trial that you mentioned. But I don't know when I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, prior -- prior to your investigation, and specifically your interview with -- with the decedent, you gathered as much information as you could with regard to Idriz Balaj because, among other things, you were concerned as to whether or not Idriz Balaj was involved in any of the matters that you were investigating; correct?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that, sir, because I was also involved in other investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. Were you tasked to speak to the decedent by your team leader, Mr. Raatikainen?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the time that you were tasked to speak with the decedent, was there a discussion concerning the -- the importance of meeting with this individual and discussing what information he could give to you?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at my recollection, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Did you keep any notes independent of the reports that you wrote concerning your contact with the decedent? Any notes, personal notes that you memorialised, or rough notes with regard to your contact with the decedent, specifically with regard to the photo-spread procedure that you engaged in?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And finally, with regard to the identification procedure, was anyone else present apart from yourself, the decedent, and the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody else was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you were speaking to the decedent, you were speaking to the decedent through the interpreter; correct?

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There was no point in time when you and the decedent were speaking together --

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- in a language that you both commonly shared.

utterances.speaker: ROEL VERSONNEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The witness only spoke Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. Any questions, Mr. Harvey? Any questions, Mr. Emmerson? Any need to re-examine the witness, Mr. Re? Mr. Versonnen, this concludes your testimony. Often I say "I would like to thank you for coming a long way to The Hague," but it may not have been that long for you. Nevertheless, thank you for answering questions that were put to you. You are excused.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: One line, if I may. Before the day ends, may I formally tender D220, which was marked for identification during the testimony of Avni Krasniqi yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are -- yes, that's formally tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, we'll not deal with it at this very moment, because it's quarter past 7.00, which means that the interpreters, technicians, transcribers, security have done a great job today. It's due to them that we could finish our programme today. We adjourn until Tuesday, the 20th of November - at least, as matters stand now - Tuesday, the 20th of November, quarter past 2.00, Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 20th day of November, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 25
